summary.text: A salt marsh is a tidal wetland between land and sea, regularly flooded by salty or brackish tides and covered in salt-tolerant herbs, grasses or low shrubs.
Its plants trap and bind sediment to keep the marsh stable, and the marsh feeds coastal food webs and protects the shore.
Salt marshes form on calm temperate and high-latitude shores, while in the tropics and subtropics mangroves take their place.

facts.label: Most extensive marshes
facts.value: Outside the tropics, notably the North Atlantic

items.prompt: Why do many young marine fish spend time in salt marshes before heading to open water?

options.label: The water there is warmer than the sea
Calm water and tall grasses give them refuge
The marsh water has no salt at all
Strong currents carry food straight to them

items.explain: The low physical energy and high grasses of a salt marsh offer a refuge, and many marine fish use marshes as nursery grounds.

items.prompt: A calm, muddy tropical shoreline is flooded by the tides. What habitat usually grows there instead of a salt marsh?

options.label: Kelp forest
Coral reef
Sand dunes
Mangrove forest

items.explain: In the tropics and subtropics, salt marshes are replaced by mangroves, which are dominated by salt-tolerant trees rather than herbs.

items.prompt: Mud keeps settling on a bare tidal flat and the ground slowly rises. What does that make possible?

options.label: Tides flood it less, so plants can take hold
Waves get stronger and wash the mud away
The flat turns into a freshwater lake
Tides flood it more often and for longer

items.explain: As tidal flats gain height through sediment build-up, tidal flooding becomes less frequent and shorter, so vegetation can colonise the surface.

items.prompt: How does rising sea level put some salt marshes at risk?

options.label: It makes the water too fresh for the plants
It brings in fish that eat the grasses
It erodes them and drowns them under water
It dries them out by pulling the tide back

items.explain: Sea level rise caused by climate change endangers marshes through erosion and submersion.

items.prompt: Why do some birds raise their chicks among the tall grasses of a salt marsh?

options.label: The grasses keep the chicks warm in winter
The salty water cleans their feathers
The marsh has no other animals to compete with
It offers shelter from predators and plenty of food

items.explain: The marsh gives birds both sanctuary from predators and abundant food such as trapped fish, insects, shellfish and worms.

items.prompt: Sticky mats of blue-green algae spread over bare mud on a tidal flat. How do they help a marsh begin?

options.label: They block sunlight so mud stays wet
They hold fine sediment and help it build up
They soak up salt so seeds can sprout
They feed the fish that plant the seeds

items.explain: The algae fix silt and clay particles to their sticky sheaths, making sediment resist erosion and helping it accumulate so colonising plants can grow.
